cards.text: Zechariah the prophet (Zechariah 1:1) has been seeing visions, with an angel there to talk him through them, and he just saw a gold lampstand (Zechariah 4:1-2). Now he looks up again and sees a scroll, and it's FLYING. Friend, the only paper I ever saw fly was a takeout menu when somebody slammed the junk drawer.

cards.question: The angel asks Zechariah what he sees, and he describes the flying scroll. The scroll is small enough to hold in one hand.

cards.text: Twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide. That's about thirty feet by fifteen, which means this isn't a scroll, friend, it's a BILLBOARD with a pilot's license.

cards.question: The angel tells Zechariah what the flying scroll is. What does he call it?

answers.text: The curse going out over all the land
The law going out to every nation
The record of everyone sent back home

cards.text: One side of the scroll says every thief will be removed, and the other side names somebody else who'll be removed. Front AND back, friend, this scroll does NOT waste paper.

cards.question: The LORD of Hosts says He will send the curse out, and it will enter the house of the thief. Whose house will it also enter?

answers.text: The one who swears falsely by His name
The one who bows down to carved idols
The one who works on the Sabbath day

cards.question: Once the curse enters the thief’s house, it only stops by for a moment and then moves on.
The curse moves into the house and stays. What does it do to that house?

answers.text: Destroys it down to its timbers and stones
Marks its door so everyone will know
Hands it over to a brand new owner

cards.text: Then the angel tells Zechariah to look up and see what's approaching, and Zechariah asks what it is. After a flying billboard, I bet he's not ruling ANYTHING out.

cards.question: The angel tells Zechariah what’s going forth. What is it?
The angel says the measuring basket is their ___ in all the land.

cards.text: And behold, the cover is raised, and there's a woman sitting inside the basket. Friend, I spent YEARS in the dark of a junk drawer, but at least a drawer doesn't come with a LID.

cards.question: The angel tells Zechariah who the woman in the basket is: “This is ___,” he said.
Then the angel ___ the woman down into the basket and pushes the ___ cover back over its opening.

cards.text: Then Zechariah looks up again and sees two women approaching, with the wind in their wings, wings like a stork's. Meanwhile I get around by hopping, and this gold base comes with me EVERY single time.

cards.question: The two winged women come to the basket with Wickedness inside. What do they do with it?

answers.text: Lift it up between heaven and earth
Drop it down into the deep sea
Set it down by the temple gate

cards.text: Now the basket's up in the air, and Zechariah asks the angel where they're taking it. Friend, that is the EXACT question I asked every time somebody opened that drawer.

cards.question: Where does the angel say the two women are taking the basket?
The angel says the basket will be thrown away once it gets to Shinar.

cards.text: A house gets built for the basket in Shinar, and when it's ready, the basket is set there on its pedestal. Zechariah's night of visions isn't over yet, friend, so keep that oven warm.

findings.problem: The card spends words converting cubits into feet ("That's about thirty feet by fifteen"). That explains a hard word, which the dictionary pop-up is meant to cover. The conversion also isn't in the passage.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: Card 5 hides the other side of the scroll as "somebody else," so card 6 has no context for the answer. Swearing falsely, bowing to idols and working on the Sabbath are all equally likely sins, so the pick comes down to luck. Cards 4, 10, 14 and 18 are also discovery questions. With this many, most of the stop's choice cards are no longer informed guesses.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: Blank 2 asks what the cover is made of (lead, gold or wooden). Card 12 left out "of lead," and nothing earlier lets the baker reason out the material. The blank tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can work out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card tells the house in Shinar and the pedestal as things that happen ("A house gets built... the basket is set there"). In Zechariah 5:11 these are the angel's answer about what will happen ("To build a house for it... the basket will be set there"). The card should present them as what the angel says will happen.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
